title: The Cher Episode
summary: Josh and Chuck (with iHeart Intro voice) profile Cher's life and career: her childhood and early performing ambitions, relationships with Warren Beatty and Sonny Bono, the Sonny & Cher duo and their TV variety shows, Bob Mackie's costume collaborations, her divorce and the exploitative Share Enterprises contract, her solo comebacks in the 1980s and 1998 with Believe and Auto-Tune, her Oscar snub for Mask, her gay icon status, and her activism and charity work. The episode also covers a listener mail anecdote about payphone dime-back hacks.

entities.name: Come Back to the Five and Dime, Jimmy Dean, Jimmy Dean

segments.title: Opening banter and Cher's family background
segments.summary: Hosts open with banter about a dog and an auto-tune joke, then introduce Cher's Armenian heritage, her father John Paul Sarkisian, her mother Georgia Holt, and her early life.

segments.title: Childhood ambitions and Warren Beatty
segments.summary: Cher wanted to perform from a young age, inspired by Dumbo, and at eleven staged Oklahoma playing the male roles herself. At sixteen she met Warren Beatty, who dated her with her mother's approval.

segments.title: Meeting Sonny Bono and singing with Phil Spector
segments.summary: Cher dropped out of high school and moved in with Sonny Bono, marrying in a ceremony in 1964 that was not legal until 1969. Sonny worked for Phil Spector, and Cher sang backup on hits by the Righteous Brothers and the Ronettes.

segments.title: Solo debut, Bonnie Joe Mason, and Sonny & Cher hits
segments.summary: Cher debuted as Bonnie Joe Mason with Ringo I Love You, signed with Imperial Records, and scored a hit with a cover of Dylan's All I Really Want to Do. As Caesar and Cleo, then Sonny & Cher, they hit number one with I Got You Babe, helped by the Rolling Stones in England.
topics: All I Really Want to Do cover

segments.title: Sonny & Cher Comedy Hour and TV success
segments.summary: The duo's comic banter defined them, and they became TV stars through guest spots and a CBS show starting in 1971 that drew large audiences. Their variety format and costumes by Bob Mackie are discussed.

segments.title: Bob Mackie and costume collaboration
segments.summary: Bob Mackie designed Cher's over-the-top costumes from the TV show onward, and the hosts discuss their close creative partnership. A short aside checks whether Mackie is still alive; he is 84.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Ad break for the show's sponsors.

segments.title: Divorce, Chastity, and the Share Enterprises contract
segments.summary: The marriage deteriorated as both spouses had affairs. Sonny financed the 1969 film Chastity, which flopped. In the divorce Cher learned Sonny owned most of Share Enterprises and that her contract barred outside work; David Geffen helped her get out and sign with Warner Brothers.

segments.title: Sonny & Cher Show ends and early solo albums
segments.summary: Cher's 1975 solo variety show was less popular, and the duo split professionally by 1977. Her album Gypsys, Tramps and Thieves came out in 1971; the hosts discuss the song Half-Breed and its controversy, and her later headdress performance.

segments.title: Naked dress and Met Gala
segments.summary: Cher's sheer naked dress at the 1974 Met Gala, escorted by Bob Mackie, caused a major stir and was featured on the cover of Time the next year.

segments.title: Greg Allman marriage and son Elijah Blue
segments.summary: Cher married Allman Brothers Band founder Greg Allman in Vegas shortly after her divorce was final. Their volatile marriage produced son Elijah Blue Allman in 1976, and the hosts discuss his struggles and a conservatorship attempt.

segments.title: Name change and dating history
segments.summary: In 1978 Cher legally changed her name to Cher. The hosts list her high-profile boyfriends, including Gene Simmons, Val Kilmer, Tom Cruise and Eric Stoltz, and discuss Stoltz's history as the original Marty McFly.
topics: Eric Stoltz Back to the Future

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Ad break for the show's sponsors.

segments.title: Acting career: Broadway, Silkwood, Mask, and the Oscar snub
segments.summary: Cher moved into acting in the 1980s with Come Back to the Five and Dime, Jimmy Dean, Jimmy Dean, which won her a Golden Globe. She then starred in Silkwood and Mask, won the Best Actress award at Cannes for Mask, and was not nominated for an Oscar; she won Best Actress the next year for Moonstruck.
topics: Come Back to the Five and Dime

segments.title: Revenge gown and Oscars presenting
segments.summary: Bob Mackie designed a feathered gown for Cher's presenting appearance at the Oscars, which the hosts describe as a statement after the snub. They discuss who won the Best Actress award that year.

segments.title: Mask movie aside
segments.summary: A brief tangent where the hosts confuse the film Mask with Jim Carrey's The Mask, and Chuck mentions rewatching Mask.

segments.title: 1980s comeback, Believe and Auto-Tune
segments.summary: Cher's 1980s and 1989 albums revived her music career. Her 1998 hit Believe, produced by Mark Taylor, used Auto-Tune in an extreme way and was a number one single; Warner Brothers US had passed on the album, but the UK label released it.

segments.title: Auto-Tune legacy and seven decades of hits
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the lasting use of Auto-Tune in music, including Jay Z's comments on it. Cher is described as the only solo artist with hits in seven decades, which is why her perfume is named Decades.

segments.title: Recent work: Vegas residency, albums, Christmas album
segments.summary: Cher held a Las Vegas residency at Caesar's Palace from 2008 to 2011, released a dance album in 2013 and a Christmas album most recently. The hosts also discuss the Broadway musical The Cher Show.

segments.title: Gay icon status, activism and charity
segments.summary: Cher explained her loyal gay fan base in an interview, and the hosts recount her childhood encounter with gay men. They note her advocacy for trans rights after Chaz Bono's transition, her support for veterans with helmet inserts, and her co-founding of the Free the Wild charity.

segments.title: Listener mail: payphone dime hack
segments.summary: A listener named Danielle describes an old payphone trick for getting coins back by controlling the dial return after dialing nine. The hosts thank her and invite listener anecdotes.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts close with the show's standard sign-off and iHeartRadio credit.
